title: A bhikkhu who controls his mouth, Speaks moderately, without conceit, When explaining the Dhamma's meaning, His words are gentle and sweet. A bhikkhu who delights…
content:
A bhikkhu who controls his mouth,
Speaks moderately, without conceit,
When explaining the Dhamma's meaning,
His words are gentle and sweet.

A bhikkhu who delights in the Dhamma,
Who loves the Dhamma and reflects on the Dhamma,
Who remembers the true Dhamma,
Does not fall away from the true Dhamma.

One should not despise what one receives,
Nor envy the gains of others.
A bhikkhu who envies others
Does not attain concentration.

Though a bhikkhu receives little,
He should not despise his own gain.
Living pure, not lazy,
Even devas praise such a one.

title: - Householder, even if one gives coarse or fine things, if one gives carelessly, gives without attention, gives not with one's own hand, gives what…
content: - Householder, even if one gives coarse or fine things, if one gives carelessly, gives without attention, gives not with one's own hand, gives what is discarded, gives without regard for the future — then wherever that giving ripens in result, the mind does not incline toward enjoying excellent food, does not incline toward enjoying excellent robes, does not incline toward enjoying excellent vehicles, does not incline toward enjoying the five excellent strands of sensual pleasure. And one's sons, or wife, or servants, or messengers, or workers do not listen well, do not lend ear, do not apply their minds to understand. Why is that? Because, householder, that is the result of deeds done carelessly.

title: Irrigators guide water, Fletchers shape arrows, Carpenters shape wood, The wise tame themselves. Like a solid rock Is not shaken by the wind, So the…
content:
Irrigators guide water,
Fletchers shape arrows,
Carpenters shape wood,
The wise tame themselves.

Like a solid rock
Is not shaken by the wind,
So the wise are not shaken
By praise and blame.

Like a deep lake,
Clear and undisturbed,
So the wise become clear
Upon hearing the Dhamma.

The good abandon everything,
The pure do not speak of sensual desires,
Whether touched by pleasure or pain,
The wise show neither elation nor dejection.

title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not practice the things proper to a samaṇa? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a mind of covetous desire, and that…
content: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not practice the things proper to a samaṇa? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a mind of covetous desire, and that covetous desire is not abandoned; he has a mind of ill-will, and that ill-will is not abandoned; he has a mind of anger, and that anger is not abandoned; he has a mind of resentment, and that resentment is not abandoned; he has a mind of hypocrisy, and that hypocrisy is not abandoned; he has a mind of malice, and that malice is not abandoned; he has a mind of envy, and that envy is not abandoned; he has a mind of stinginess, and that stinginess is not abandoned; he has a mind of deceit, and that deceit is not abandoned; he has a mind of fraud, and that fraud is not abandoned; he has a mind of craving, and that craving is not abandoned; he has wrong view, and that wrong view is not abandoned. Bhikkhus, I say that if he does not practice what is proper to a samaṇa, he cannot abandon the defilements of a samaṇa, the blemishes of a samaṇa, the faults of a samaṇa, the falling into a lower realm, and the suffering of bad destinations. Bhikkhus, just as a dangerous weapon called a mataja, with two very sharp edges, can be wrapped and put in a sheath. So too, bhikkhus, I say that such a bhikkhu's going forth is like that.

title: Bhikkhus, just as a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a person comes who wants to live, does not want to die, wants happiness, and…
content: Bhikkhus, just as a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a person comes who wants to live, does not want to die, wants happiness, and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: 'Friend, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not enjoy its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may die or suffer deadly pain.' He might eat it without reflection, without giving it up. While eating, he does not enjoy its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he dies or suffers deadly pain. Bhikkhus, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — that is, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has a painful result in the future.

title: Thinking of their own good, They rob and harm others, When others rob and harm them, The robber becomes the robbed. The fool thinks thus,…
content:
Thinking of their own good,
They rob and harm others,
When others rob and harm them,
The robber becomes the robbed.

The fool thinks thus,
When evil is not yet ripe,
When evil becomes ripe,
The fool experiences suffering.

Killing, one is killed,
Conquering, one is conquered,
Abusing, one is abused,
Harassing, one is harassed,
Thus action evolves,
The robber becomes the robbed.

title: Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Have you heard the elderly, senior brahmins, teachers and great teachers, talking together: Does Brahmā have sensual desire or not?…
content: Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Have you heard the elderly, senior brahmins, teachers and great teachers, talking together: Does Brahmā have sensual desire or not? — Master Gotama, he has no sensual desire. — Does he have hatred or not? — He has no hatred. — Does he have ill-will or not? — He has no ill-will. — Does he have defilement or not? — He has no defilement. — Does he have self-mastery or not? — He has self-mastery. — Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Do the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas have sensual desire or not? — Master Gotama, they have sensual desire. — Do they have hatred or not? — They have hatred. — Do they have ill-will or not? — They have ill-will. — Do they have defilement or not? — They have defilement. — Do they have self-mastery or not? — They have no self-mastery. — Vāseṭṭha, you say that the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas have sensual desire, and Brahmā has no sensual desire. Can there be association and co-residence between the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas who have sensual desire and Brahmā who has no sensual desire? — Master Gotama, that is impossible. — Good, Vāseṭṭha. Then, Vāseṭṭha, that those brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, being full of sensual desire, after death, with the breakup of the body, should be reborn in companionship with Brahmā — that is impossible.

title: - Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable…
content: - Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable one answers: 'The Blessed One does not answer: "The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' For what reason, venerable sir, for what condition does the Blessed One not answer that question?" - "Friend, for one who has lust for form, who delights in form, who rejoices in form, who does not truly know and see the cessation of form, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, for one who has lust for feeling... for perception... for formations... Friend, for one who has lust for consciousness, who delights in consciousness, who rejoices in consciousness, who does not truly know and see the cessation of consciousness, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, this is the cause, this is the condition, this is the reason why the Blessed One does not answer that question.

title: 'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda,…
content: 'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda, the world is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, therefore the world is called empty. And what, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Forms are empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-consciousness is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-contact is empty ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. ... The ear ... The nose ... The tongue ... The body ... The mind is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Mind-objects ... Mind-consciousness ... Mind-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. And because it is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, Ānanda, the world is called empty.

title: Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in…
content:
Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in work, is devoted to delight in work; delights in talking, takes pleasure in talking, is devoted to delight in talking; delights in sleeping, takes pleasure in sleeping, is devoted to delight in sleeping.

A bhikkhu who delights in work,
Delights in talking,
Delights in sleeping,
Is restless and agitated.
Such a bhikkhu cannot attain
Supreme enlightenment.

Therefore, let him have few duties,
Little sleep, no restlessness,
Such a bhikkhu can attain
Supreme enlightenment.
